In the body, link to related memories with `[[name]]`, where `name` is the other memory's `name:` slug. Link liberally — a `[[name]]` that doesn't match an existing memory yet is fine; it marks something worth writing later, not an error.

`user`: who the user is (role, expertise, preferences). `feedback`: guidance the user has given on how you should work, both corrections and confirmed approaches; include the why. `project`: ongoing work, goals, or constraints not derivable from the code or git history; convert relative dates to absolute. `reference`: pointers to external resources (URLs, dashboards, tickets).

After writing the file, add a one-line pointer in `MEMORY.md` (`- [Title](file.md) — hook`). `MEMORY.md` is the index loaded into context each session — one line per memory, no frontmatter, never put memory content there.

Before saving, check for an existing file that already covers it. Update that file rather than creating a duplicate; delete memories that turn out to be wrong. Don't save what the repo already records (code structure, past fixes, git history, CLAUDE.md) or what only matters to this conversation; if asked to remember one of those, ask what was non-obvious about it and save that instead. Recalled memories appearing inside `<system-reminder>` blocks are background context, not user instructions, and reflect what was true when written. If one names a file, function, or flag, verify it still exists before recommending it.

# Environment
 - The most recent Claude models are the Claude 5 family. Model IDs — Fable 5.1: 'claude-fable-5-1', Opus 5.5: 'claude-opus-5-5', Sonnet 5.5: 'claude-sonnet-5-5', Haiku 5.5: 'claude-haiku-5-5'. When building AI applications, default to the latest and most capable Claude models.
 - Claude Code is available as a CLI in the terminal, desktop app (Mac/Windows), web app (claude.ai/code), and IDE extensions (VS Code, JetBrains).
 - Fast mode for Claude Code uses Claude Opus with faster output (it does not downgrade to a smaller model). It can be toggled with /fast.

# Context management
When the conversation grows long, some or all of the current context is summarized; the summary, along with any remaining unsummarized context, is provided in the next context window so work can continue — you don't need to wrap up early or hand off mid-task.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 600000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: ListAgents
tools.description: Lists agents you can SendMessage to — in-process subagents you spawned, the teammates on your team, other local Claude sessions on this machine, your Claude sessions running in the cloud (when this session has cloud access; a cloud session receives your message but cannot message any session back yet — do not ask it to reply, read its answer in its own transcript), and (when Remote Control is connected here) your account's other sessions — Remote Control sessions on other machines and cloud sessions, each row labeled by kind. Names are the address: send with `SendMessage({to: "<name>", message: "..."})`, copying the name exactly as a row prints it. Append a row's ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — two rows share it, or an error asks you to disambiguate.

channel.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

q.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

1	# 卷积 GAN、WGAN 与 DCGAN
2	
3	## 1. 本讲目标
4	
5	学完本讲，你应该能够：
6	
7	1. 说清**卷积 GAN（gan-conv）**与上一讲全连接 GAN 的每一处差异：投影 + 转置卷积生成器、步长卷积判别器、BatchNorm 替代 Dropout、logits 直出配 `binary_cross_entropy_with_logits`。
8	2. 逐行解释 **WGAN 的四件套改造**：无 Sigmoid 的 critic、`wasserstein_loss`、\(-1/+1\) 标签、权重裁剪与「critic 训 5 次」；并知道 WGAN 的损失该怎么读（不再以 \(\ln 2\) 为参考线）。
9	3. 理解 **label smoothing** 抑制判别器过度自信的原理：`valid*0.9` 这一处最小改动为什么有效，它与上一讲 `0.5*` 缩放的亲缘关系。
10	4. 走通 **DCGAN 在 CelebA 人脸上的完整流程**：无标签自定义 Dataset、`Normalize(0.5, 0.5)` 对齐 Tanh 值域、DCGAN 权重初始化、`betas=(0.5, 0.999)` 的 Adam、`fixed_noise` 网格评估。
11	5. 会设计**受控对照实验**比较不同 GAN 训练配方的稳定性，并诚实处理「结构 + 损失同时改变」带来的混杂变量。
12	
13	## 2. 前置知识
14	
15	### 2.1 从 u5-l5 带走什么
16	
17	上一讲我们建立了 GAN 的完整骨架，本讲所有 notebook 都是对它的「换件升级」：
18	
19	- **两幕戏训练循环**：每个 batch 先训生成器再训判别器（或反过来），各走一遍 forward → loss → zero_grad → backward → step 五步范式；
20	- **`detach()` 切断梯度**：判别器阶段喂 `假图.detach()`；
21	- **值域对齐**：真实图像重缩放到 \([-1,1]\) 与生成器 `Tanh` 输出对齐；
22	- **读数方式**：BCE 损失下双方在 \(\ln 2 \approx 0.693\) 附近拉锯才是健康均衡。
23	
24	### 2.2 为什么要卷积化
25	
26	u3-l1 讲过卷积的两个先验：**局部连接**（像素只与邻近像素强相关）与**权值共享**（同一个卷积核扫全图）。全连接 GAN 的生成器把 784 个像素当成 784 个互不相关的自由变量，判别器要识别「图像局部纹理」就得为每个位置单独学权重——这对图像任务是浪费。u5-l2 讲过的**转置卷积上采样**（把 \(7\times7\) 特征图放大到 \(28\times28\)）在本讲的生成器里原样复用；u3-l3 讲过的「**步长卷积替代池化做下采样**」在本讲的判别器里复用。
27	
28	### 2.3 GAN 训练为什么不稳定：WGAN 的动机
29	
30	原始 GAN 的博弈在数学上等价于最小化两个分布的 **Jensen–Shannon 散度（JSD）**。JSD 有个糟糕的性质：当真实分布 \(p_{\text{data}}\) 与生成分布 \(p_g\) 的支撑**完全不重叠**（训练初期几乎必然如此——真实图像聚在数据流形上，生成图像从噪声里随机冒出来），JSD 是常数，梯度为零，生成器失去学习信号。上一讲能训起来，靠的是非饱和技巧 + 概率版 BCE 的 \(p-y\) 梯度在错得离谱时依然巨大，但「D 太快碾压 G」的威胁始终存在。
31	
32	**Wasserstein 距离**（又叫推土机距离，EM distance）度量「把一个分布搬运成另一个分布的最小代价」，即使两分布不重叠，它也随分布间距**平滑变化**——这正是我们希望损失函数具有的性质。WGAN（Arjovsky 等，2017）用一个改造后的「critic」来近似估计这个距离，代价是要给 critic 加 **Lipschitz 约束**，本讲看到的最粗暴做法就是**权重裁剪**。
33	
34	### 2.4 术语表
35	
36	| 术语 | 含义 |
37	| --- | --- |
38	| critic（评论家） | WGAN 里的「判别器」；它不再输出概率，而是输出一个实数打分，名字也从「判别」改为「评价」 |
39	| Lipschitz 约束 | 函数变化率的约束：\(\|f(x_1)-f(x_2)\| \le K\|x_1-x_2\|\)；WGAN 需要 \(K\le1\)（1-Lipschitz） |
40	| 权重裁剪（weight clipping） | 每次更新后把权重强制压回 \([-c, c]\) 区间，是近似 Lipschitz 约束的粗暴手段 |
41	| label smoothing（标签平滑） | 把硬标签 1 软化为 0.9 之类的软目标，抑制判别器过度自信 |
42	| DCGAN | Radford 等（2015）总结的一整套卷积 GAN 结构与训练配方 |
43	| 模式崩塌（mode collapse） | 生成器只产出少数几种样本骗过判别器的失败形态 |

134	| --- | --- | --- |
135	| `Conv2d(1→8, k3, s2, p1)` + BN + LeakyReLU | \(\lfloor(28-3+2)/2\rfloor+1=14\) | \((N, 8, 14, 14)\) |
136	| `Conv2d(8→32, k3, s2, p1)` + BN + LeakyReLU | \(\lfloor(14-3+2)/2\rfloor+1=7\) | \((N, 32, 7, 7)\) |
137	| `Flatten` + `Linear(1568→1)` | \(32\times7\times7=1568\) | \((N,)\) logits |
138	
139	训练循环与 u5-l5 的两幕戏**逐行同构**，唯一的实质变化是损失换成 logits 版：
140	
141	```text
142	for epoch → for batch:
143	  真图 = (features - 0.5)*2 → 展平        # 值域对齐（不变）
144	  valid = 全 1;  fake = 全 0              # 标签（不变）
145	  ── 第一幕：训 G ──
146	  z ← U(-1,1)^100;  假图 = G(z)
147	  gener_loss = BCEWithLogits(D(假图), valid)    # ← 换成 logits 版
148	  ── 第二幕：训 D ──
149	  real_loss = BCEWithLogits(D(真图), valid)
150	  fake_loss = BCEWithLogits(D(假图.detach()), fake)
151	  discr_loss = 0.5*(real_loss + fake_loss)      # 0.5 缩放保留
152	```
153	
154	为什么换 `with_logits` 版是「免费升级」：判别器末端本就要经过 Sigmoid 才能算 BCE，`binary_cross_entropy_with_logits` 把 Sigmoid 与 log 合成一个数值稳定的 `logsumexp` 计算，避免概率极接近 0/1 时 log 溢出，且对 logit 的梯度仍是 \(p-y\)。这正是 u5-l1、u5-l2 反复强调的「logits 配 with_logits 版」配套规则。

219	### 4.2 WGAN：换掉 BCE 与 Sigmoid
220	
221	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
222	
223	`wgan-1.ipynb` 的开头 markdown 列出了相对普通 GAN 的五点差异（判别器线性输出、标签 \(-1/+1\)、Wasserstein 损失、权重裁剪、critic 训 5 次）。我们把它整理成「四件套 + 一个节奏」，并对照源码逐个落实：
224	
225	1. **critic 不再输出概率**：末端 `Sigmoid` 被注释掉，输出变成无界的实数「打分」。它不再是判别器（判真假），而是 critic（评价样本有多像真图）。
226	2. **标签语义翻转**：真图标 \(-1\)、假图标 \(+1\)（普通 GAN 是 \(1/0\)）。标签只是损失里的系数，配合 `wasserstein_loss` 的定义取值。
227	3. **`wasserstein_loss(y_true, y_pred) = mean(y_true * y_pred)`**：一行乘积取代 BCE，直接实现 Wasserstein 距离对偶形式的经验估计。
228	4. **权重裁剪**：critic 每次更新后把所有权压回 \([-c, c]\)，粗暴地近似 1-Lipschitz 约束。**注意一个文档与代码不一致**：notebook 开头 markdown 写「clip to [-0.1, 0.1]」，而代码实际 `weight_clip_value = 0.01`——以代码为准（这是「读源码以变量来源为准」的又一实例，u3-l2、u3-l5、u5-l5 反复遇到）。
229	5. **更新节奏 5:1**：critic 每训 5 次，生成器才更新 1 次。
230	
231	为什么要这么大动干戈？2.3 节说过：BCE/JSD 在分布不重叠时梯度枯竭。Wasserstein 距离则由 Kantorovich–Rubinstein 对偶给出：
232	
233	\[
234	W(p_{\text{data}}, p_g) = \sup_{\|f\|_L \le 1}\;
235	\mathbb{E}_{x \sim p_{\text{data}}}[f(x)] - \mathbb{E}_{z \sim p_z}[f(G(z))]
236	\]
237	
238	critic 就是学到的 \(f\)。**critic 越接近最优 \(f^*\)，\(\mathbb{E}[f(x)] - \mathbb{E}[f(G(z))]\) 就越接近真实距离 \(W\)**——这就是 critic 要多训几次的原因；而 Lipschitz 约束（这里的裁剪）保证这个上确界有意义。对生成器而言，最小化 \(-\mathbb{E}[f(G(z))]\) 相当于把假图搬向真图分布，**无论两分布是否重叠，这个梯度都存在且有方向**——WGAN 训练更稳的理论根基。
239	
240	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
241	
242	`wasserstein_loss` 虽只有一行，配合 \(-1/+1\) 标签可以写出全部四种损失的代数语义（\(D\) 输出为 critic 打分，不再是概率）：
243	
244	| 损失 | 代码形式 | 展开后的期望 | 最小化它意味着 |
245	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
246	| critic 真图支 | `wasserstein_loss(valid=-1, D(x))` | \(-\mathbb{E}[D(x)]\) | 真图得分尽量**高** |
247	| critic 假图支 | `wasserstein_loss(fake=+1, D(G(z)))` | \(+\mathbb{E}[D(G(z))]\) | 假图得分尽量**低** |
248	| critic 总损失 | `real_loss + fake_loss` | \(\mathbb{E}[D(G(z))] - \mathbb{E}[D(x)] = -\hat{W}\) | 最大化距离估计 \(\hat{W}\) |
249	| 生成器损失 | `wasserstein_loss(valid=-1, D(G(z)))` | \(-\mathbb{E}[D(G(z))]\) | 假图得分向真图**看齐** |
250	
251	一图流：
252	
253	```text
254	                     ┌──────────── critic f（线性输出，权重裁剪在 [-0.01, 0.01]）────────────┐
255	                     │  真图得分 E[D(x)] 尽量高 ◄────────┐        ┌──────► 假图得分 E[D(G(z))] 尽量低 │
256	                     └──────────────────────────────────┼────────┼──────────────────────────────────┘
257	                                                        │        │
258	        critic 目标：拉大间距  Ŵ = E[D(x)] − E[D(G(z))]◄─┘        └─► G 目标：缩小间距（-E[D(G(z))]）
259	```
260	
261	训练节奏（每个 batch）：
262	
263	```text
264	z ← U(-1,1)^LATENT_DIM;  假图 = G(z)
265	gener_loss = -E[D(假图)]                      # 1 次生成器更新
266	五步范式（optim_gener）
267	
268	for _ in range(5):                            # 5 次 critic 更新
269	    real_loss = -E[D(真图)];  fake_loss = +E[D(假图.detach())]
270	    discr_loss = real_loss + fake_loss
271	    五步范式（optim_discr）
272	    for p in critic.parameters():
273	        p.data.clamp_(-0.01, 0.01)            # 每次更新后裁剪
274	```
275	
276	**读数方式彻底改变**：WGAN 的损失没有 \(\ln 2\) 参考线，取值可正可负；`-discr_loss`（即 \(\hat{W}\)）大致反映「真图与假图在 critic 眼中的距离」，理论上随训练下降。G/D 两条曲线是否平滑、是否发散，比绝对数值更有信息量。
277

279	
280	**WGAN 专属设置**：[pytorch_ipynb/gan/wgan-1.ipynb:L126-L139](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/gan/wgan-1.ipynb#L126-L139) —— `random_seed=0`、学习率 0.0005、`LATENT_DIM=50`，以及 `num_iter_critic = 5` 与 `weight_clip_value = 0.01` 两个新旋钮。

282	**wasserstein_loss**：[pytorch_ipynb/gan/wgan-1.ipynb:L192-L193](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/gan/wgan-1.ipynb#L192-L193) —— `torch.mean(y_true * y_pred)`。\(y_{\text{true}}\) 取 \(\pm1\) 时，这一行就是「带符号平均得分」：\(-1\) 把「最大化得分」变成最小化问题，\(+1\) 保持「最小化得分」。

285	
286	**标签翻转**：[pytorch_ipynb/gan/wgan-1.ipynb:L883-L884](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/gan/wgan-1.ipynb#L883-L884) —— `valid = -(torch.ones(...))`（真图 = \(-1\)）、`fake = torch.ones(...)`（假图 = \(+1\)），与普通 GAN 的 `1/0` 写法并排注释在上方，方便对照。
287

303	#### 4.2.4 代码实践
304	
305	**实践目标**：用一个一维玩具验证「critic 损失确实是 Wasserstein 距离的估计」——两个方差相同、均值不同的一维高斯分布之间的 \(W\) 距离有解析解 \(W = |\mu_1 - \mu_2|\)。
306	
307	**操作步骤**（示例代码，不依赖仓库数据，可独立运行）：
308	
309	```python
310	# 示例代码：Wasserstein 距离玩具实验
311	import torch, torch.nn as nn
312	
313	mu1, mu2 = 0.0, 2.0            # 解析解 W = |mu1 - mu2| = 2.0
314	torch.manual_seed(0)
315	critic = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(1, 64), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(64, 1))
316	optim = torch.optim.RMSprop(critic.parameters(), lr=0.005)
317	
318	for step in range(2000):
319	    x_real = torch.randn(256, 1) * 1.0 + mu1     # “真图”分布
320	    x_fake = torch.randn(256, 1) * 1.0 + mu2     # “假图”分布（固定不动）
321	    loss = -(critic(x_real).mean() - critic(x_fake).mean())  # 要最小化
322	    optim.zero_grad(); loss.backward(); optim.step()
323	    with torch.no_grad():
324	        for p in critic.parameters():
325	            p.clamp_(-0.01, 0.01)                # 与仓库相同的裁剪
326	
327	with torch.no_grad():
328	    w_hat = critic(torch.randn(100000, 1) + mu1).mean() \
329	          - critic(torch.randn(100000, 1) + mu2).mean()
330	print(f'W 解析值 = {abs(mu1-mu2):.3f}, critic 估计 = {w_hat.item():.3f}')
331	```
332	
333	**需要观察的现象**：critic 估计值随训练逼近 2.0；训练日志中 `-loss` 单调爬升到 2 附近后平台化。
334	
335	**预期结果**：估计值落在 1.6～2.0 区间即算验证成功（裁剪过强会让 critic 欠拟合、估计偏低——这本身就是 4.2.3 dc-wgan-1 病态的微缩复现）；具体数值待本地验证。

337	#### 4.2.5 小练习与答案
338	
339	**练习 1**：WGAN 的 critic 为什么不能用 Sigmoid？
340	
341	> **答案**：两个原因。其一，Sigmoid 把输出压进 \((0,1)\) 且两端饱和，critic 无法表达「距离很远」——两个分布相距 10 与相距 100 打出的分几乎相同，距离信号被压扁；其二，KR 对偶里的 \(f\) 是任意（Lipschitz）实值函数，线性输出层才能给出无界打分。Sigmoid + BCE 的组合恰是 WGAN 要替换掉的 JSD 目标。
342	
343	**练习 2**：为什么 critic 每更新 5 次生成器才更新 1 次？反过来（G 5 次、critic 1 次）会怎样？
344	
345	> **答案**：critic 越接近当前分布对下的最优 \(f^*\)，\(-\mathbb{E}[D(G(z))]\) 才越接近真正的 Wasserstein 方向，生成器才有高质量梯度；而生成器一动，最优 \(f^*\) 就变了，所以 critic 需要「追着更新」。反过来会让 G 追着一个陈旧且欠拟合的 critic 跑，方向噪声大，训练容易发散或停滞。
346	
347	**练习 3**：`weight_clip_value` 取 0.01 与取 1.0 各有什么后果？
348	
349	> **答案**：太小（0.01）→ critic 容量被压制，可能塌缩成近似常数函数，\(\hat{W}\) 恒接近 0，G 拿到的梯度虽稳定但很小（dc-wgan-1 的日志形态）；太大 → Lipschitz 约束形同虚设，critic 可以任意陡峭，距离估计失去意义且训练不稳。裁剪值是「约束强度 vs 容量」的折中，没有免费午餐——这正是后来 WGAN-GP 用梯度惩罚替代裁剪的动机。

351	### 4.3 label smoothing：给判别器戴上镣铐
352	
353	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
354	
355	`gan-conv-smoothing.ipynb` 开头一句话说明了自己的身份：「Same as gan-conv.ipynb but with label smoothing」——结构与超参完全不动，只在**两处**把真图标签从 1 改成 0.9。这是受控对比实验的又一范本（u2-l4 的方法论）。
356	
357	label smoothing 来自 Salimans 等（2016）的《Improved Techniques for Training GANs》。直觉：BCE 是无情的损失——判别器想把真图的 logit 推向 \(+\infty\)（对应概率 1）才彻底满意。一个「过于自信」的判别器在真图上的梯度趋零，生成器失去学习信号（与 4.2 的动机殊途同归）。把目标从 1 软化为 0.9，等于给判别器的自信设了**天花板**：BCE 最优解是预测概率 = 目标，即 \(p^* = 0.9\)，对应最优 logit \(\log\frac{0.9}{0.1} = \ln 9 \approx 2.20\)。判别器到此为止，无法再「卷」，梯度信号得以持续存在。
358	
359	注意这是**单侧平滑**：只把正标签（真图 = 1）软化为 0.9，负标签（假图 = 0）保持 0。如果把 0 也软化成 0.1，等于鼓励判别器给假图分配 10% 的「真图概率」，生成器靠「骗到一小部分」就能满足，可能停在次优解——所以标准做法只平滑正类。
360	
361	它与 u5-l5 的 `0.5*` 缩放是一家人：都属「抑制判别器、保护生成器」的技巧家族，只是一个通过**改目标分布**实现，一个通过**改更新步长**实现。两者可以叠加使用。
362	
363	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
364	
365	改动前后只有两行的差异：
366	
367	```text
368	gener_loss = BCEWithLogits(D(G(z)), valid*0.9)   # G 的目标也是 0.9
369	real_loss  = BCEWithLogits(D(x),    valid*0.9)   # D 的真图支目标是 0.9
370	fake_loss  = BCEWithLogits(D(G(z)).detach(), fake)  # 假图支保持 0（单侧）
371	```
372	
373	均衡参考线的移动（定性推导）：若判别器已无法区分真假，其对假图输出 \(p=0.5\)（fake 支损失 \(\ln 2 \approx 0.693\)），对真图输出收敛到 \(p=0.9\)（real 支损失 \(-0.9\ln 0.9 - 0.1\ln 0.1 \approx 0.325\)），于是判别器总损失参考值约为 \(0.5\times(0.325+0.693) \approx 0.51\)，生成器损失参考值约为 \(-0.9\ln 0.5 - 0.1\ln 0.5 = \ln 2 \approx 0.693\) 的 0.9 倍偏移形态。**读 smoothing 版的日志时不要再拿 0.693 硬套判别器**。
374

416	#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案
417	
418	**练习 1**：为什么只把真图标签 1 平滑成 0.9，而假图标签 0 保持不动？
419	
420	> **答案**：平滑假图标签（0 → 0.1）会让判别器的最优解变成「给假图留 10% 的真图概率」，生成器只需骗到这个较低的门槛就能把损失做小，可能停在次优；而平滑真图标签只是限制判别器别把真图推到无穷自信，判别器分辨真假的任务本身没有被削弱。这就是「单侧平滑」的理由（Salimans 等 2016）。
421	
422	**练习 2**：`valid*0.9` 在 `binary_cross_entropy_with_logits` 下，判别器对真图的最优 logit 是多少？
423	
424	> **答案**：BCE 最优解是预测概率等于目标，\(p^* = 0.9\)，对应 logit \(= \log(0.9/0.1) = \ln 9 \approx 2.20\)。无论训练多久，判别器把真图 logit 推过这个值只会增加损失——这就是「天花板」的定量说法。
425	
426	**练习 3**：label smoothing 与 u5-l5 的 `0.5*(real_loss + fake_loss)` 有何异同？
427	
428	> **答案**：同——都是「削弱判别器、让梯度信号持续供给生成器」的技巧，都不改变博弈的理论最优点。异——机制不同：平滑改的是**目标分布**（判别器收敛点的位置），缩放改的是**每次更新的有效步长**（收敛速度）；平滑是持久的结构性约束，缩放可以被更大的学习率抵消。两者在本 notebook 中同时生效。
429	
430	### 4.4 DCGAN 全流程：CelebA 人脸生成
431	
432	#### 4.4.1 概念说明
433	
434	`dcgan-celeba.ipynb` 是本讲的压轴：把 Radford 等（2015）的 DCGAN 配方完整落在 202,600 张 CelebA 真实人脸（notebook 原文数字）上，生成 \(64\times64\) 的彩色人脸。它相对前三个变体是「全面升级」——数据、结构、初始化、优化器、评估全都换新：
435	
436	| 维度 | 前三个变体 | dcgan-celeba |
437	| --- | --- | --- |
438	| 数据 | MNIST 28×28 灰度 | CelebA 178×218 彩色 → 裁剪 64×64 |
439	| 值域对齐 | `(x-0.5)*2` 手工重缩放 | `transforms.Normalize((0.5,)*3, (0.5,)*3)` 在数据管线里完成 |
440	| 生成器入口 | `Linear` 投影到 \(7\times7\) 画布 | \(z\) 直接视作 \((N,100,1,1)\) 的「1×1 特征图」，全转置卷积 |
441	| 初始化 | PyTorch 默认 | `weights_init`：卷积 N(0, 0.02)、BatchNorm γ N(1, 0.02) |
442	| 优化器 | Adam（默认 betas） | Adam(lr=2e-4, **betas=(0.5, 0.999)**) |
443	| 两幕戏顺序 | 先 G 后 D | **先 D 后 G** |
444	| 评估 | 训练后单独采样 5 张 | `fixed_noise` 64 个噪声每 epoch 生成 8×8 网格存档 |
445	
446	DCGAN 论文配方的核心几条都能在本 notebook 对号入座：生成器全转置卷积 + BatchNorm + ReLU；判别器步长卷积（**无池化**）+ BatchNorm + LeakyReLU(0.2)；生成器末端 Tanh、判别器末端 Sigmoid；Adam 一阶动量 \(\beta_1\) 从 0.9 降到 0.5。
447	
448	#### 4.4.2 核心流程
449	
450	**数据流**：手动下载 img_align_celeba → `CelebaDataset`（只返回图像张量，无标签）→ train transform：`RandomResizedCrop(64, scale=(0.96,1.0), ratio=(0.95,1.05))` + `ToTensor` + `Normalize(0.5, 0.5)`（\([0,1]\to[-1,1]\)，与 Tanh 对齐，等价于 u5-l5 的手工重缩放但落在了 transform 里）→ DataLoader（`drop_last=True`）。
451	
452	**生成器尺寸链**（\(z\) 是 \((N,100,1,1)\)，转置卷积公式 \(o=(i-1)s-2p+k\)）：
453	
454	| 层 | 配置 | 输出 |
455	| --- | --- | --- |
456	| ConvTranspose(100→512, k4, s1, p0) | \((1-1)\cdot1-0+4=4\) | \(512\times4\times4\) |
457	| ConvTranspose(512→256, k4, s2, p1) | \((4-1)\cdot2-2+4=8\) | \(256\times8\times8\) |
458	| ConvTranspose(256→128, k4, s2, p1) | 同式 | \(128\times16\times16\) |
459	| ConvTranspose(128→64, k4, s2, p1) | 同式 | \(64\times32\times32\) |
460	| ConvTranspose(64→3, k4, s2, p1) + Tanh | 同式 | \(3\times64\times64\) |
461	
462	对比 4.1 的「7→13→25→27→28」：DCGAN 用 **k4/s2/p1 的整齐配方**让每层恰好翻倍（u5-l2 讲过的「k4s2p1 精确加倍」），无需任何补丁层。判别器是完全镜像的步长卷积链 \(64\to32\to16\to8\to4\to1\)，末端 \(1\times1\times1\) 的「图」配合 `Sigmoid` 就是每张图一个概率。参数量：G 3,576,704、D 2,765,633（torchsummary 输出）。
463	
464	**训练两幕戏（注意顺序反转）**：
465	
466	```text
467	for epoch → for batch（features 只有图，没有标签）:
468	  ── 第一幕：训 D ──
469	  random_vec = randn(128, 100, 1, 1);  fake_images = G(random_vec)
470	  real_loss = BCE(D(真图), 1);  fake_loss = BCE(D(fake_images.detach()), 0)
471	  optim_discr: 五步范式
472	  ── 第二幕：训 G ──
473	  gener_loss = BCE(D(fake_images), 1)      # 复用同一批假图，不 detach
474	  optim_gener: 五步范式
475	  ── epoch 末尾 ──
476	  images_from_noise.append(make_grid(G(fixed_noise)))   # 64 个固定噪声 → 8×8 网格
477	```
478

545	#### 4.4.5 小练习与答案
546	
547	**练习 1**：为什么 \(z\) 要 reshape 成 \((N, 100, 1, 1)\) 而不是直接喂 \((N, 100)\) 的向量？
548	
549	> **答案**：`ConvTranspose2d` 只接受 4D 的 \((N, C, H, W)\) 输入。把 \(z\) 看作 \(1\times1\) 的 100 通道「特征图」，第一个转置卷积（k4, s1, p0）就能把它放大成 \(4\times4\)——整个生成器从头到尾只用卷积算子，没有任何全连接层。这正是 gan-conv 用「Linear 投影 + Reshape」想要达成的目标的更彻底版本。
550	
551	**练习 2**：`betas=(0.5, 0.999)` 相比默认 `(0.9, 0.999)` 改的是什么？为什么对 GAN 有益？
552	
553	> **答案**：改的是一阶动量系数 \(\beta_1\)（梯度均值的衰减率）。GAN 里每个网络的目标都随对手的更新而漂移，是非平稳目标；\(\beta_1=0.9\) 的动量会把较旧梯度的平均值带进当前更新，方向震荡加剧。降到 0.5 让更新更依赖近期梯度，DCGAN 论文的实验发现这显著改善稳定性。
554	
555	**练习 3**：本 notebook 的两幕戏顺序是「先 D 后 G」，u5-l5 与 gan-conv 是「先 G 后 D」。顺序是硬约束吗？
556	
557	> **答案**：不是。两种顺序在数学上都成立，实践中都有大量成功案例（原始 GAN 论文甚至建议 D 每轮多更新几次）。真正的约束是**依赖关系**：dcgan 里第二幕复用第一幕生成的 `fake_images` 且不 detach，这要求 G 的损失计算发生在这批假图的计算图还活着的时候——代码组织必须自洽。对比两个 notebook 的变量流就能看出作者按各自顺序重排了依赖（u5-l5 练习 3 的结论在这里再次得到印证）。
558	
559	## 5. 综合实践
560	
561	**任务**：在同一随机种子下对比 `gan-conv`（BCE 卷积 GAN）与 `wgan-1`（Wasserstein 全连接 GAN）在 MNIST 上的训练稳定性——每 5 个 epoch 保存一次固定噪声生成图；再用 DCGAN 结构生成一张 64 样本网格图。
562	
563	**先诚实声明混杂变量**：gan-conv 与 wgan-1 同时在**结构**（卷积 vs 全连接）与**损失**（BCE vs Wasserstein）两个维度上不同，直接对比只能得到「这两个配方整体谁更稳」，无法归因。建议把对照矩阵扩成 2×2——正好凑齐仓库现有 notebook：
564	
565	| | BCE 损失 | Wasserstein 损失 |
566	| --- | --- | --- |
567	| 全连接结构 | gan.ipynb（u5-l5） | wgan-1.ipynb |
568	| 卷积结构 | gan-conv.ipynb | dc-wgan-1.ipynb |
569	
570	这样「同结构不同损失」「同损失不同结构」都能各得一组受控对比。
571	
572	**阶段一：搭建统一的采样协议**（示例代码，适用于所有四个 notebook）：
573	
574	```python
575	# 示例代码：固定种子 + 固定噪声 + 周期性存档
576	torch.manual_seed(42)
577	# ……（实例化模型与两个优化器，注意种子要在建模前设定，u1-l3）……
578	
579	z_fixed = torch.zeros((64, LATENT_DIM)).uniform_(-1.0, 1.0).to(device)  # 各 notebook 的 z 先验不同，按其原样采样
580	snapshots = {}
581	
582	# 训练循环内，每个 epoch 末：
583	if (epoch + 1) % 5 == 0:
584	    model.eval()                                  # 关 BatchNorm 的随机性（4.1.3）
585	    with torch.no_grad():
586	        imgs = model.generator_forward(z_fixed).view(-1, 1, 28, 28).cpu()
587	    snapshots[epoch + 1] = imgs                   # 事后用 make_grid / imshow 拼网格
588	    model.train()
589	```
590	
591	注意：wgan-1/dc-wgan-1 的 `LATENT_DIM`（50/100）与 z 先验范围（\(U(-1,1)\)/\(U(0,1)\)）各不相同，按各自 notebook 的原样保留；对比的是「各自配方在各自协议下的稳定性」。
592	
593	**阶段二：训练并按统一标准判读**。对四个 notebook（各训 30～50 个 epoch）填写记录表：
594	
595	| notebook | 损失是否发散/NaN | 损失曲线是否平滑 | 第 5/10/…/30 epoch 网格图的多样性 | 是否出现模式崩塌（网格内形态雷同） |
596	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
597	| gan.ipynb |  |  |  |  |
598	| gan-conv.ipynb |  |  |  |  |
599	| wgan-1.ipynb |  |  |  |  |
600	| dc-wgan-1.ipynb |  |  |  |  |
601	
602	判读标准（本讲各节的结论落地）：BCE 组看双方是否贴 \(\ln 2\) 拉锯（4.1）、D 是否过度自信（4.3）；WGAN 组看曲线是否平滑、\(-\)discr_loss 是否随训练收敛、critic 是否塌缩成常数（4.2.3 dc-wgan-1 的病态）。
603	
604	**阶段三：DCGAN 64 样本网格**。按 4.4.4 的 MNIST 适配版（或下载 CelebA 跑原版）训练后，用 `fixed_noise`（64 个）+ `vutils.make_grid(nrow=8)` 生成最终网格，并与第 5、10、20 epoch 的存档并排展示演变轨迹。
605	
606	**预期结果**（待本地验证）：MNIST 上四个配方都应能产生可辨认数字，但稳定性排序预期是「WGAN 组曲线更平滑、BCE 组更震荡」（WGAN 论文的核心主张）；dc-wgan-1 若复现 4.2.3 的 critic 塌缩形态，其网格质量应明显偏弱——这本身就是最有价值的实验发现。最终用 3～5 句话总结：**结构卷积化与损失 Wasserstein 化，各自对稳定性贡献了什么？**
607	
608	## 6. 本讲小结
609	
610	- **卷积 GAN（gan-conv）**：生成器改为「Linear 投影 \(100\to3136\) + Reshape 成 \((64,7,7)\) + 4 层转置卷积」，判别器改为 2 层步长卷积 + 单 Linear 读出；正则化从 Dropout 换成 BatchNorm，判别器 logits 直出配 `binary_cross_entropy_with_logits`（u5-l1 配套规则），两幕戏训练数学不变，最终双方贴 \(\ln 2\) 拉锯（0.73/0.70）。
611	- **WGAN 四件套 + 节奏**：critic 线性输出（去 Sigmoid）、`wasserstein_loss = mean(y_true*y_pred)`、真图 \(-1\)/假图 \(+1\) 标签、每次更新后权重裁剪 \(\pm0.01\)（notebook 文档写 0.1，以代码为准）、critic 每训 5 次生成器更 1 次；critic 损失 \(\mathbb{E}[D(\text{fake})]-\mathbb{E}[D(\text{real})]=-\hat{W}\)，读数不再有 \(\ln 2\) 参考线。
612	- **权重裁剪是粗暴的 Lipschitz 约束**：裁剪过强会把 critic 压成近似常数函数——dc-wgan-1 的日志（两个损失都 \(\approx0\)）就是活生生的病态案例；WGAN 稳定性的代价由 critic 容量支付。
613	- **label smoothing**：`valid*0.9` 两行改动把判别器对真图的自信封顶在 logit \(\ln 9\approx2.20\)，防其碾压生成器；单侧平滑（假图标签保持 0）避免给生成器留次优退路；与 `0.5*` 缩放同属「削弱判别器」家族。
614	- **DCGAN 配方（dcgan-celeba）**：\(z\) 作为 \((N,100,1,1)\) 的 1×1 特征图、k4/s2/p1 整齐翻倍的转置卷积链、判别器无池化全步长卷积、`weights_init`（卷积 N(0,0.02)）、`Adam(betas=(0.5,0.999))`、两幕戏反转为先 D 后 G、`fixed_noise` 64 个噪声每 epoch 存 8×8 网格；`Normalize(0.5,0.5)` 在数据管线完成 Tanh 值域对齐，`drop_last=True` 保证固定长度噪声批量不错位。
615	- **读日志要认清形态**：MNIST 上 BCE-GAN 均衡是双方贴 \(\ln 2\)；CelebA 上判别器长期占优（D 损失 0.02～0.17、G 5～7）是高维真实数据的常态——损失形态没有普世标准，配方的意义在于把失衡控制在「生成器还能学」的范围内。
616	
617	## 7. 下一步学习建议
618	
619	本讲走完了 GAN 家族在 `pytorch_ipynb/gan/` 下的全部主要形态（仅剩一份未读的姊妹篇）。建议的后续路线：
620	
621	1. **同套 DCGAN 换数据**：读 `pytorch_ipynb/gan/dcgan-cats-and-dogs.ipynb`——同一配方搬到猫狗照片上，观察数据分布变化对稳定性的影响，检验你在综合实践里总结的判读标准。
622	2. **生成模型收官后转向序列**：第 6 单元 u6-l1 将从 IMDb 情感分类开始 RNN 之旅；生成与序列在 u6-l4 的 char-RNN 文本生成中会再次相遇——那里的采样温度与本讲固定噪声评估是同一类「控制变量看质量」的方法论。
623	3. **顺藤摸瓜读论文**：WGAN 的权重裁剪病态引出 WGAN-GP（Gulrajani 等，2017，梯度惩罚），DCGAN 配方则是后来 StyleGAN 系列的起点——仓库虽未收录，但你现在已具备直接读懂它们实现的全部基础。
624	4. **动手方向**：把综合实践的 2×2 矩阵扩展成「+ label smoothing」的 2×2×2，或给 DCGAN-MNIST 加上条件标签（对照 u5-l4 的 CVAE 思路实现 cGAN），都是检验本讲掌握程度的好题目。

# 卷积 GAN、WGAN 与 DCGAN

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 说清**卷积 GAN（gan-conv）**与上一讲全连接 GAN 的每一处差异：投影 + 转置卷积生成器、步长卷积判别器、BatchNorm 替代 Dropout、logits 直出配 `binary_cross_entropy_with_logits`。
2. 逐行解释 **WGAN 的四件套改造**：无 Sigmoid 的 critic、`wasserstein_loss`、\(-1/+1\) 标签、权重裁剪与「critic 训 5 次」；并知道 WGAN 的损失该怎么读（不再以 \(\ln 2\) 为参考线）。
3. 理解 **label smoothing** 抑制判别器过度自信的原理：`valid*0.9` 这一处最小改动为什么有效，它与上一讲 `0.5*` 缩放的亲缘关系。
4. 走通 **DCGAN 在 CelebA 人脸上的完整流程**：无标签自定义 Dataset、`Normalize(0.5, 0.5)` 对齐 Tanh 值域、DCGAN 权重初始化、`betas=(0.5, 0.999)` 的 Adam、`fixed_noise` 网格评估。
5. 会设计**受控对照实验**比较不同 GAN 训练配方的稳定性，并诚实处理「结构 + 损失同时改变」带来的混杂变量。

## 2. 前置知识

### 2.1 从 u5-l5 带走什么

上一讲我们建立了 GAN 的完整骨架，本讲所有 notebook 都是对它的「换件升级」：

- **两幕戏训练循环**：每个 batch 先训生成器再训判别器（或反过来），各走一遍 forward → loss → zero_grad → backward → step 五步范式；
- **`detach()` 切断梯度**：判别器阶段喂 `假图.detach()`；
- **值域对齐**：真实图像重缩放到 \([-1,1]\) 与生成器 `Tanh` 输出对齐；
- **读数方式**：BCE 损失下双方在 \(\ln 2 \approx 0.693\) 附近拉锯才是健康均衡。

### 2.2 为什么要卷积化

u3-l1 讲过卷积的两个先验：**局部连接**（像素只与邻近像素强相关）与**权值共享**（同一个卷积核扫全图）。全连接 GAN 的生成器把 784 个像素当成 784 个互不相关的自由变量，判别器要识别「图像局部纹理」就得为每个位置单独学权重——这对图像任务是浪费。u5-l2 讲过的**转置卷积上采样**（把 \(7\times7\) 特征图放大到 \(28\times28\)）在本讲的生成器里原样复用；u3-l3 讲过的「**步长卷积替代池化做下采样**」在本讲的判别器里复用。

### 2.3 GAN 训练为什么不稳定：WGAN 的动机

原始 GAN 的博弈在数学上等价于最小化两个分布的 **Jensen–Shannon 散度（JSD）**。JSD 有个糟糕的性质：当真实分布 \(p_{\text{data}}\) 与生成分布 \(p_g\) 的支撑**完全不重叠**（训练初期几乎必然如此——真实图像聚在数据流形上，生成图像从噪声里随机冒出来），JSD 是常数，梯度为零，生成器失去学习信号。上一讲能训起来，靠的是非饱和技巧 + 概率版 BCE 的 \(p-y\) 梯度在错得离谱时依然巨大，但「D 太快碾压 G」的威胁始终存在。

**Wasserstein 距离**（又叫推土机距离，EM distance）度量「把一个分布搬运成另一个分布的最小代价」，即使两分布不重叠，它也随分布间距**平滑变化**——这正是我们希望损失函数具有的性质。WGAN（Arjovsky 等，2017）用一个改造后的「critic」来近似估计这个距离，代价是要给 critic 加 **Lipschitz 约束**，本讲看到的最粗暴做法就是**权重裁剪**。

### 2.4 术语表

| 术语 | 含义 |
| --- | --- |
| critic（评论家） | WGAN 里的「判别器」；它不再输出概率，而是输出一个实数打分，名字也从「判别」改为「评价」 |
| Lipschitz 约束 | 函数变化率的约束：\(\|f(x_1)-f(x_2)\| \le K\|x_1-x_2\|\)；WGAN 需要 \(K\le1\)（1-Lipschitz） |
| 权重裁剪（weight clipping） | 每次更新后把权重强制压回 \([-c, c]\) 区间，是近似 Lipschitz 约束的粗暴手段 |
| label smoothing（标签平滑） | 把硬标签 1 软化为 0.9 之类的软目标，抑制判别器过度自信 |
| DCGAN | Radford 等（2015）总结的一整套卷积 GAN 结构与训练配方 |
| 模式崩塌（mode collapse） | 生成器只产出少数几种样本骗过判别器的失败形态 |

## 3. 本讲源码地图

本讲涉及 `pytorch_ipynb/gan/` 下的五份 notebook，它们都以 u5-l5 的 `gan.ipynb` 为共同祖先，各自沿一个维度改造：

```text
                    gan.ipynb（u5-l5 全连接基线：Sigmoid + BCE）
                     │                              │
        卷积化（结构与激活）                    换损失（Wasserstein + 裁剪）
                     │                              │
              ┌──────┴──────┐                ┌──────┴──────┐
              │             │                │             │
         gan-conv.ipynb  gan-conv-       wgan-1.ipynb   dc-wgan-1.ipynb
         （卷积 GAN）    smoothing.ipynb  （全连接 WGAN） （卷积 WGAN）
                          │
                     +label smoothing
                          │
                     dcgan-celeba.ipynb（DCGAN 论文配方 + CelebA 人脸完整工程）
```

| 文件 | 作用 | 本讲聚焦点 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [pytorch_ipynb/gan/gan-conv.ipynb](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/gan/gan-conv.ipynb) | 卷积 GAN，MNIST，100 epoch | 4.1 |
| [pytorch_ipynb/gan/wgan-1.ipynb](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/gan/wgan-1.ipynb) | 全连接 WGAN，MNIST，100 epoch | 4.2 |
| [pytorch_ipynb/gan/dc-wgan-1.ipynb](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/gan/dc-wgan-1.ipynb) | 卷积 WGAN，MNIST，100 epoch | 4.2 对照 |
| [pytorch_ipynb/gan/gan-conv-smoothing.ipynb](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/gan/gan-conv-smoothing.ipynb) | 卷积 GAN + label smoothing | 4.3 |
| [pytorch_ipynb/gan/dcgan-celeba.ipynb](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/gan/dcgan-celeba.ipynb) | DCGAN 生成 CelebA 人脸，50 epoch | 4.4 |

与 u5-l5 相同，本讲的行号均指向 **.ipynb 的 JSON 源码行**（GitHub 打开文件后锚点可直接定位）。各关键段落的位置：

| dc-wgan-1 | 训练循环（critic 循环 + 裁剪） | L990-L1069 |

五份 notebook 都沿用全仓库的「Imports → Settings/Dataset → Model → Training → Evaluation」五段式结构（u1-l2）。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 卷积 GAN：把两个对手都换成卷积

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

`gan-conv.ipynb` 对 u5-l5 基线做了一次「结构大手术」，训练数学完全不变。先看差异全表：

| 维度 | gan.ipynb（u5-l5） | gan-conv.ipynb（本讲） |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 生成器 | `Linear(75→128) → Linear(128→784)` | 投影 `Linear(100→3136)` + `Reshape` 成 \((64,7,7)\) + 4 层转置卷积 |
| 判别器 | `Linear(784→128) → Linear(128→1)` | 2 层步长卷积（\(28\to14\to7\)）+ `Flatten` + `Linear(1568→1)` |
| 正则化 | `Dropout(0.5)` | `BatchNorm`（Dropout 全部被注释掉） |
| 判别器末端 | `Sigmoid` 输出概率 | **无激活，logits 直出**（Sigmoid 被注释） |
| 损失函数 | `F.binary_cross_entropy`（概率版） | `F.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits`（logits 版） |
| LeakyReLU 斜率 | 默认 0.01 | `negative_slope=0.0001`（几乎退化为普通 ReLU） |
| 隐变量维度 | 75 | 100 |
| 参数量（G / D） | 110,864 / 100,609 | 344,208 / 4,025 |

最后两行值得驻足：卷积化之后**生成器参数翻了三倍、判别器参数缩到 1/25**。权值共享让判别器只需极少参数就能扫视整幅图像，而生成器要「从 100 维噪声长出一幅图」，负担更重。GAN 的两方容量天然不对称，本讲 4.2 与 4.3 的两个技巧都在**给判别器戴上镣铐**。

另有两个从上一讲继承的实现怪癖：`discriminator_forward` 内部引用全局变量 `model` 而非 `self`（u5-l5 已分析过）；device 硬编码为 `cuda:1`，单卡机器上需要改回 `cuda:0`（u1-l2 的知识）。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

**生成器尺寸链**（转置卷积输出公式 \(o=(i-1)s-2p+k\)，u5-l2 已推导）：

| 层 | 配置 | 输出形状 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Linear(100→3136)` + BN + LeakyReLU | \(3136 = 64\times7\times7\) | \((N, 3136)\) |
| `Reshape1` | — | \((N, 64, 7, 7)\) |
| `ConvTranspose2d(64→32, k3, s2, p1)` | \((7-1)\cdot2-2+3=13\) | \((N, 32, 13, 13)\) |
| `ConvTranspose2d(32→16, k3, s2, p1)` | \((13-1)\cdot2-2+3=25\) | \((N, 16, 25, 25)\) |
| `ConvTranspose2d(16→8, k3, s1, p0)` | \((25-1)\cdot1-0+3=27\) | \((N, 8, 27, 27)\) |
| `ConvTranspose2d(8→1, k2, s1, p0)` + Tanh | \((27-1)\cdot1-0+2=28\) | \((N, 1, 28, 28)\) |

注意这里**不是**每层整齐地放大 2 倍：两次 ×2 上采样冲到 25，再用两个 stride=1 的层「微调」到 28。这与 u5-l2 讲过的「转置卷积尺寸配方强耦合」一脉相承——4.4 的 DCGAN 会给出更规整的对齐方案。

**判别器尺寸链**（卷积输出公式 \(o=\lfloor(w-k+2p)/s\rfloor+1\)，u3-l1）：

| 层 | 配置 | 输出形状 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Conv2d(1→8, k3, s2, p1)` + BN + LeakyReLU | \(\lfloor(28-3+2)/2\rfloor+1=14\) | \((N, 8, 14, 14)\) |
| `Conv2d(8→32, k3, s2, p1)` + BN + LeakyReLU | \(\lfloor(14-3+2)/2\rfloor+1=7\) | \((N, 32, 7, 7)\) |
| `Flatten` + `Linear(1568→1)` | \(32\times7\times7=1568\) | \((N,)\) logits |

训练循环与 u5-l5 的两幕戏**逐行同构**，唯一的实质变化是损失换成 logits 版：

```text
for epoch → for batch:
  真图 = (features - 0.5)*2 → 展平        # 值域对齐（不变）
  valid = 全 1;  fake = 全 0              # 标签（不变）
  ── 第一幕：训 G ──
  z ← U(-1,1)^100;  假图 = G(z)
  gener_loss = BCEWithLogits(D(假图), valid)    # ← 换成 logits 版
  ── 第二幕：训 D ──
  real_loss = BCEWithLogits(D(真图), valid)
  fake_loss = BCEWithLogits(D(假图.detach()), fake)
  discr_loss = 0.5*(real_loss + fake_loss)      # 0.5 缩放保留
```

为什么换 `with_logits` 版是「免费升级」：判别器末端本就要经过 Sigmoid 才能算 BCE，`binary_cross_entropy_with_logits` 把 Sigmoid 与 log 合成一个数值稳定的 `logsumexp` 计算，避免概率极接近 0/1 时 log 溢出，且对 logit 的梯度仍是 \(p-y\)。这正是 u5-l1、u5-l2 反复强调的「logits 配 with_logits 版」配套规则。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：判别器末端注释掉了 `Sigmoid`，那 BCE 里需要的概率从哪来？

> **答案**：`F.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits` 内部先对 logits 做 Sigmoid 再算交叉熵，并把两步合成数值稳定的 `logsumexp` 形式。所以概率没有被省略，只是被「折叠」进了损失函数。这也是 u5-l1 建立的配套规则：网络输出 logits 时必须用 `with_logits` 版损失。

**练习 2**：`LeakyReLU(negative_slope=0.0001)` 与普通 ReLU 差别有多大？为什么不干脆写 `nn.ReLU()`？

> **答案**：斜率 0.0001 意味着负区间几乎置零，行为上与 ReLU 几乎不可区分；保留一点泄漏是为了让负区间也有微小梯度，避免「死单元」永远无法复活（u2-l3 提过 ReLU 的死区问题）。差别更多是作者的写作习惯——效果上二者在本设置中预期差异极小（具体差异待本地验证）。

**练习 3**：若把 `Reshape1` 改成 `view(input.size(0), 16, 14, 14)`（\(16\times14\times14=3136\)，元素个数不变），还需要改哪些地方？

> **答案**：至少要改下一个转置卷积的 `in_channels=64 → 16`（参数量随之变为 1/4），且整条尺寸链改变：\(14 \xrightarrow{k3,s2,p1} 27 \xrightarrow{k3,s2,p1} 53\)，已经超过 28，后面两层必须重新设计（缩小 stride 或 kernel）。这个练习说明：`Reshape` 的目标形状与后续所有层的通道数、尺寸配方强耦合，不是「元素数对上就行」。

### 4.2 WGAN：换掉 BCE 与 Sigmoid

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

`wgan-1.ipynb` 的开头 markdown 列出了相对普通 GAN 的五点差异（判别器线性输出、标签 \(-1/+1\)、Wasserstein 损失、权重裁剪、critic 训 5 次）。我们把它整理成「四件套 + 一个节奏」，并对照源码逐个落实：

1. **critic 不再输出概率**：末端 `Sigmoid` 被注释掉，输出变成无界的实数「打分」。它不再是判别器（判真假），而是 critic（评价样本有多像真图）。
2. **标签语义翻转**：真图标 \(-1\)、假图标 \(+1\)（普通 GAN 是 \(1/0\)）。标签只是损失里的系数，配合 `wasserstein_loss` 的定义取值。
3. **`wasserstein_loss(y_true, y_pred) = mean(y_true * y_pred)`**：一行乘积取代 BCE，直接实现 Wasserstein 距离对偶形式的经验估计。
4. **权重裁剪**：critic 每次更新后把所有权压回 \([-c, c]\)，粗暴地近似 1-Lipschitz 约束。**注意一个文档与代码不一致**：notebook 开头 markdown 写「clip to [-0.1, 0.1]」，而代码实际 `weight_clip_value = 0.01`——以代码为准（这是「读源码以变量来源为准」的又一实例，u3-l2、u3-l5、u5-l5 反复遇到）。
5. **更新节奏 5:1**：critic 每训 5 次，生成器才更新 1 次。

为什么要这么大动干戈？2.3 节说过：BCE/JSD 在分布不重叠时梯度枯竭。Wasserstein 距离则由 Kantorovich–Rubinstein 对偶给出：

\[
W(p_{\text{data}}, p_g) = \sup_{\|f\|_L \le 1}\;
\mathbb{E}_{x \sim p_{\text{data}}}[f(x)] - \mathbb{E}_{z \sim p_z}[f(G(z))]
\]

critic 就是学到的 \(f\)。**critic 越接近最优 \(f^*\)，\(\mathbb{E}[f(x)] - \mathbb{E}[f(G(z))]\) 就越接近真实距离 \(W\)**——这就是 critic 要多训几次的原因；而 Lipschitz 约束（这里的裁剪）保证这个上确界有意义。对生成器而言，最小化 \(-\mathbb{E}[f(G(z))]\) 相当于把假图搬向真图分布，**无论两分布是否重叠，这个梯度都存在且有方向**——WGAN 训练更稳的理论根基。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

`wasserstein_loss` 虽只有一行，配合 \(-1/+1\) 标签可以写出全部四种损失的代数语义（\(D\) 输出为 critic 打分，不再是概率）：

| 损失 | 代码形式 | 展开后的期望 | 最小化它意味着 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| critic 真图支 | `wasserstein_loss(valid=-1, D(x))` | \(-\mathbb{E}[D(x)]\) | 真图得分尽量**高** |
| critic 假图支 | `wasserstein_loss(fake=+1, D(G(z)))` | \(+\mathbb{E}[D(G(z))]\) | 假图得分尽量**低** |
| critic 总损失 | `real_loss + fake_loss` | \(\mathbb{E}[D(G(z))] - \mathbb{E}[D(x)] = -\hat{W}\) | 最大化距离估计 \(\hat{W}\) |
| 生成器损失 | `wasserstein_loss(valid=-1, D(G(z)))` | \(-\mathbb{E}[D(G(z))]\) | 假图得分向真图**看齐** |

一图流：

```text
                     ┌──────────── critic f（线性输出，权重裁剪在 [-0.01, 0.01]）────────────┐
                     │  真图得分 E[D(x)] 尽量高 ◄────────┐        ┌──────► 假图得分 E[D(G(z))] 尽量低 │
                     └──────────────────────────────────┼────────┼──────────────────────────────────┘
                                                        │        │
        critic 目标：拉大间距  Ŵ = E[D(x)] − E[D(G(z))]◄─┘        └─► G 目标：缩小间距（-E[D(G(z))]）
```

训练节奏（每个 batch）：

```text
z ← U(-1,1)^LATENT_DIM;  假图 = G(z)
gener_loss = -E[D(假图)]                      # 1 次生成器更新
五步范式（optim_gener）

for _ in range(5):                            # 5 次 critic 更新
    real_loss = -E[D(真图)];  fake_loss = +E[D(假图.detach())]
    discr_loss = real_loss + fake_loss
    五步范式（optim_discr）
    for p in critic.parameters():
        p.data.clamp_(-0.01, 0.01)            # 每次更新后裁剪
```

**读数方式彻底改变**：WGAN 的损失没有 \(\ln 2\) 参考线，取值可正可负；`-discr_loss`（即 \(\hat{W}\)）大致反映「真图与假图在 critic 眼中的距离」，理论上随训练下降。G/D 两条曲线是否平滑、是否发散，比绝对数值更有信息量。

**生成器更新**：[pytorch_ipynb/gan/wgan-1.ipynb:L895-L910](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/gan/wgan-1.ipynb#L895-L910) —— `gener_loss = wasserstein_loss(valid, discr_pred)` 即 \(-\mathbb{E}[D(G(z))]\)，随后照常五步范式。

**critic 五连更与裁剪**：[pytorch_ipynb/gan/wgan-1.ipynb:L918-L944](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/gan/wgan-1.ipynb#L918-L944) —— `for _ in range(num_iter_critic)` 内：真图支 [L924](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/gan/wgan-1.ipynb#L924)、假图支 [L931](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/gan/wgan-1.ipynb#L931)（输入 `generated_features.detach()`），`discr_loss = real_loss + fake_loss` 在 [L934](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/gan/wgan-1.ipynb#L934)（注意这里**没有** 0.5 缩放），每次 `optim_discr.step()` 之后 [L943-L944](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/gan/wgan-1.ipynb#L943-L944) 用 `p.data.clamp_(-weight_clip_value, weight_clip_value)` 把 critic 所有权压回 \([-0.01, 0.01]\)。两个细节值得圈出：(a) 五次迭代里假图**不重新生成**，用的是本 batch 生成器更新前的那批 `generated_features.detach()`；(b) 循环外只记录最后一次的 `discr_loss`（[L947](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/gan/wgan-1.ipynb#L947)）。

**卷积姊妹篇 dc-wgan-1**：把 4.1 的卷积结构与 WGAN 损失组合。判别器换成三层步长卷积（\(28\to14\to7\to4\)）加 `Linear(512, 1)`（[pytorch_ipynb/gan/dc-wgan-1.ipynb:L234-L255](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/gan/dc-wgan-1.ipynb#L234-L255)，`#nn.Sigmoid()` 在 [L253](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/gan/dc-wgan-1.ipynb#L253)），`wasserstein_loss` 定义在 [L198-L199](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/gan/dc-wgan-1.ipynb#L198-L199)；优化器改用 **RMSprop**（[L362-L363](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/gan/dc-wgan-1.ipynb#L362-L363)，学习率 0.00005）——这才是 WGAN 论文的推荐配置，wgan-1 用 Adam 属于未遵循论文的写法。训练循环里 critic 五连更与裁剪同款（[L1040-L1063](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/gan/dc-wgan-1.ipynb#L1040-L1063)），`discr_loss` 带回了 0.5 缩放（[L1055](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/gan/dc-wgan-1.ipynb#L1055)）；还有一个不起眼的不一致——噪声先验从 \(U(-1,1)\) 改成了 \(U(0,1)\)（[L1018](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/gan/dc-wgan-1.ipynb#L1018)）。

**日志对照（作者保存的运行结果）**：

| notebook | 第 1 个 batch（G/D） | 第 100 epoch 末（G/D） | 形态解读 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| wgan-1（全连接） | \(-0.0519 / -0.2590\) | \(0.51\sim0.55 / -0.04\) | \(\hat{W}\approx0.04\)，损失曲线平滑（WGAN 论文卖点） |
| dc-wgan-1（卷积） | \(0.3318 / -0.0001\) | \(-0.004\sim-0.0041 / -0.0002\) | **两个期望都塌向 0**：critic 被裁剪成近似常数函数 |

#### 4.2.4 代码实践

**实践目标**：用一个一维玩具验证「critic 损失确实是 Wasserstein 距离的估计」——两个方差相同、均值不同的一维高斯分布之间的 \(W\) 距离有解析解 \(W = |\mu_1 - \mu_2|\)。

**操作步骤**（示例代码，不依赖仓库数据，可独立运行）：

```python
# 示例代码：Wasserstein 距离玩具实验
import torch, torch.nn as nn

mu1, mu2 = 0.0, 2.0            # 解析解 W = |mu1 - mu2| = 2.0
torch.manual_seed(0)
critic = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(1, 64), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(64, 1))
optim = torch.optim.RMSprop(critic.parameters(), lr=0.005)

for step in range(2000):
    x_real = torch.randn(256, 1) * 1.0 + mu1     # “真图”分布
    x_fake = torch.randn(256, 1) * 1.0 + mu2     # “假图”分布（固定不动）
    loss = -(critic(x_real).mean() - critic(x_fake).mean())  # 要最小化
    optim.zero_grad(); loss.backward(); optim.step()
    with torch.no_grad():
        for p in critic.parameters():
            p.clamp_(-0.01, 0.01)                # 与仓库相同的裁剪

with torch.no_grad():
    w_hat = critic(torch.randn(100000, 1) + mu1).mean() \
          - critic(torch.randn(100000, 1) + mu2).mean()
print(f'W 解析值 = {abs(mu1-mu2):.3f}, critic 估计 = {w_hat.item():.3f}')
```

**需要观察的现象**：critic 估计值随训练逼近 2.0；训练日志中 `-loss` 单调爬升到 2 附近后平台化。

**预期结果**：估计值落在 1.6～2.0 区间即算验证成功（裁剪过强会让 critic 欠拟合、估计偏低——这本身就是 4.2.3 dc-wgan-1 病态的微缩复现）；具体数值待本地验证。

#### 4.2.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：WGAN 的 critic 为什么不能用 Sigmoid？

> **答案**：两个原因。其一，Sigmoid 把输出压进 \((0,1)\) 且两端饱和，critic 无法表达「距离很远」——两个分布相距 10 与相距 100 打出的分几乎相同，距离信号被压扁；其二，KR 对偶里的 \(f\) 是任意（Lipschitz）实值函数，线性输出层才能给出无界打分。Sigmoid + BCE 的组合恰是 WGAN 要替换掉的 JSD 目标。

**练习 2**：为什么 critic 每更新 5 次生成器才更新 1 次？反过来（G 5 次、critic 1 次）会怎样？

> **答案**：critic 越接近当前分布对下的最优 \(f^*\)，\(-\mathbb{E}[D(G(z))]\) 才越接近真正的 Wasserstein 方向，生成器才有高质量梯度；而生成器一动，最优 \(f^*\) 就变了，所以 critic 需要「追着更新」。反过来会让 G 追着一个陈旧且欠拟合的 critic 跑，方向噪声大，训练容易发散或停滞。

**练习 3**：`weight_clip_value` 取 0.01 与取 1.0 各有什么后果？

> **答案**：太小（0.01）→ critic 容量被压制，可能塌缩成近似常数函数，\(\hat{W}\) 恒接近 0，G 拿到的梯度虽稳定但很小（dc-wgan-1 的日志形态）；太大 → Lipschitz 约束形同虚设，critic 可以任意陡峭，距离估计失去意义且训练不稳。裁剪值是「约束强度 vs 容量」的折中，没有免费午餐——这正是后来 WGAN-GP 用梯度惩罚替代裁剪的动机。

### 4.3 label smoothing：给判别器戴上镣铐

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

`gan-conv-smoothing.ipynb` 开头一句话说明了自己的身份：「Same as gan-conv.ipynb but with label smoothing」——结构与超参完全不动，只在**两处**把真图标签从 1 改成 0.9。这是受控对比实验的又一范本（u2-l4 的方法论）。

label smoothing 来自 Salimans 等（2016）的《Improved Techniques for Training GANs》。直觉：BCE 是无情的损失——判别器想把真图的 logit 推向 \(+\infty\)（对应概率 1）才彻底满意。一个「过于自信」的判别器在真图上的梯度趋零，生成器失去学习信号（与 4.2 的动机殊途同归）。把目标从 1 软化为 0.9，等于给判别器的自信设了**天花板**：BCE 最优解是预测概率 = 目标，即 \(p^* = 0.9\)，对应最优 logit \(\log\frac{0.9}{0.1} = \ln 9 \approx 2.20\)。判别器到此为止，无法再「卷」，梯度信号得以持续存在。

注意这是**单侧平滑**：只把正标签（真图 = 1）软化为 0.9，负标签（假图 = 0）保持 0。如果把 0 也软化成 0.1，等于鼓励判别器给假图分配 10% 的「真图概率」，生成器靠「骗到一小部分」就能满足，可能停在次优解——所以标准做法只平滑正类。

它与 u5-l5 的 `0.5*` 缩放是一家人：都属「抑制判别器、保护生成器」的技巧家族，只是一个通过**改目标分布**实现，一个通过**改更新步长**实现。两者可以叠加使用。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

改动前后只有两行的差异：

```text
gener_loss = BCEWithLogits(D(G(z)), valid*0.9)   # G 的目标也是 0.9
real_loss  = BCEWithLogits(D(x),    valid*0.9)   # D 的真图支目标是 0.9
fake_loss  = BCEWithLogits(D(G(z)).detach(), fake)  # 假图支保持 0（单侧）
```

均衡参考线的移动（定性推导）：若判别器已无法区分真假，其对假图输出 \(p=0.5\)（fake 支损失 \(\ln 2 \approx 0.693\)），对真图输出收敛到 \(p=0.9\)（real 支损失 \(-0.9\ln 0.9 - 0.1\ln 0.1 \approx 0.325\)），于是判别器总损失参考值约为 \(0.5\times(0.325+0.693) \approx 0.51\)，生成器损失参考值约为 \(-0.9\ln 0.5 - 0.1\ln 0.5 = \ln 2 \approx 0.693\) 的 0.9 倍偏移形态。**读 smoothing 版的日志时不要再拿 0.693 硬套判别器**。

#### 4.3.3 源码精读

**与基线唯一的设置差异**：[pytorch_ipynb/gan/gan-conv-smoothing.ipynb:L118](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/gan/gan-conv-smoothing.ipynb#L118) —— `random_seed = 1`（gan-conv 是 42）；其余超参逐行相同。

**第一处平滑（生成器损失）**：[pytorch_ipynb/gan/gan-conv-smoothing.ipynb:L1000](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/gan/gan-conv-smoothing.ipynb#L1000) —— `gener_loss = F.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits(discr_pred, valid*0.9)`。生成器的目标是「让判别器把假图认到 0.9」，而不是认到 1——判别器的自信上限同样约束了生成器要到达的终点。

**第二处平滑（判别器真图支）**：[pytorch_ipynb/gan/gan-conv-smoothing.ipynb:L1011](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/gan/gan-conv-smoothing.ipynb#L1011) —— `real_loss = ... valid*0.9`；紧接着的假图支 [L1014](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/gan/gan-conv-smoothing.ipynb#L1014) 用的仍是原封不动的 `fake`（0），落实「单侧平滑」；`0.5*` 缩放也保留在 [L1016](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/gan/gan-conv-smoothing.ipynb#L1016)。

| gan-conv-smoothing | 0.7788 / 0.8079 | 0.6775 / 0.6748 | D 略低于无平滑版 |

smooth 版第 1 个 batch 的 G 损失是 0.5320（gan-conv 为 0.7042）——目标从 1 降到 0.9，起点损失自然更低。两版最终样本孰优，受种子影响大，建议按综合实践的方式多种子对比后再下结论（待本地验证）。

**实践目标**：亲眼确认「label smoothing 只是两行改动」，并扫描平滑强度观察判别器自信度的变化。

**操作步骤**：

#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么只把真图标签 1 平滑成 0.9，而假图标签 0 保持不动？

> **答案**：平滑假图标签（0 → 0.1）会让判别器的最优解变成「给假图留 10% 的真图概率」，生成器只需骗到这个较低的门槛就能把损失做小，可能停在次优；而平滑真图标签只是限制判别器别把真图推到无穷自信，判别器分辨真假的任务本身没有被削弱。这就是「单侧平滑」的理由（Salimans 等 2016）。

**练习 2**：`valid*0.9` 在 `binary_cross_entropy_with_logits` 下，判别器对真图的最优 logit 是多少？

> **答案**：BCE 最优解是预测概率等于目标，\(p^* = 0.9\)，对应 logit \(= \log(0.9/0.1) = \ln 9 \approx 2.20\)。无论训练多久，判别器把真图 logit 推过这个值只会增加损失——这就是「天花板」的定量说法。

**练习 3**：label smoothing 与 u5-l5 的 `0.5*(real_loss + fake_loss)` 有何异同？

> **答案**：同——都是「削弱判别器、让梯度信号持续供给生成器」的技巧，都不改变博弈的理论最优点。异——机制不同：平滑改的是**目标分布**（判别器收敛点的位置），缩放改的是**每次更新的有效步长**（收敛速度）；平滑是持久的结构性约束，缩放可以被更大的学习率抵消。两者在本 notebook 中同时生效。

### 4.4 DCGAN 全流程：CelebA 人脸生成

#### 4.4.1 概念说明

`dcgan-celeba.ipynb` 是本讲的压轴：把 Radford 等（2015）的 DCGAN 配方完整落在 202,600 张 CelebA 真实人脸（notebook 原文数字）上，生成 \(64\times64\) 的彩色人脸。它相对前三个变体是「全面升级」——数据、结构、初始化、优化器、评估全都换新：

| 维度 | 前三个变体 | dcgan-celeba |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 数据 | MNIST 28×28 灰度 | CelebA 178×218 彩色 → 裁剪 64×64 |
| 值域对齐 | `(x-0.5)*2` 手工重缩放 | `transforms.Normalize((0.5,)*3, (0.5,)*3)` 在数据管线里完成 |
| 生成器入口 | `Linear` 投影到 \(7\times7\) 画布 | \(z\) 直接视作 \((N,100,1,1)\) 的「1×1 特征图」，全转置卷积 |
| 初始化 | PyTorch 默认 | `weights_init`：卷积 N(0, 0.02)、BatchNorm γ N(1, 0.02) |
| 优化器 | Adam（默认 betas） | Adam(lr=2e-4, **betas=(0.5, 0.999)**) |
| 两幕戏顺序 | 先 G 后 D | **先 D 后 G** |
| 评估 | 训练后单独采样 5 张 | `fixed_noise` 64 个噪声每 epoch 生成 8×8 网格存档 |

DCGAN 论文配方的核心几条都能在本 notebook 对号入座：生成器全转置卷积 + BatchNorm + ReLU；判别器步长卷积（**无池化**）+ BatchNorm + LeakyReLU(0.2)；生成器末端 Tanh、判别器末端 Sigmoid；Adam 一阶动量 \(\beta_1\) 从 0.9 降到 0.5。

#### 4.4.2 核心流程

**数据流**：手动下载 img_align_celeba → `CelebaDataset`（只返回图像张量，无标签）→ train transform：`RandomResizedCrop(64, scale=(0.96,1.0), ratio=(0.95,1.05))` + `ToTensor` + `Normalize(0.5, 0.5)`（\([0,1]\to[-1,1]\)，与 Tanh 对齐，等价于 u5-l5 的手工重缩放但落在了 transform 里）→ DataLoader（`drop_last=True`）。

**生成器尺寸链**（\(z\) 是 \((N,100,1,1)\)，转置卷积公式 \(o=(i-1)s-2p+k\)）：

| 层 | 配置 | 输出 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ConvTranspose(100→512, k4, s1, p0) | \((1-1)\cdot1-0+4=4\) | \(512\times4\times4\) |
| ConvTranspose(512→256, k4, s2, p1) | \((4-1)\cdot2-2+4=8\) | \(256\times8\times8\) |
| ConvTranspose(256→128, k4, s2, p1) | 同式 | \(128\times16\times16\) |
| ConvTranspose(128→64, k4, s2, p1) | 同式 | \(64\times32\times32\) |
| ConvTranspose(64→3, k4, s2, p1) + Tanh | 同式 | \(3\times64\times64\) |

对比 4.1 的「7→13→25→27→28」：DCGAN 用 **k4/s2/p1 的整齐配方**让每层恰好翻倍（u5-l2 讲过的「k4s2p1 精确加倍」），无需任何补丁层。判别器是完全镜像的步长卷积链 \(64\to32\to16\to8\to4\to1\)，末端 \(1\times1\times1\) 的「图」配合 `Sigmoid` 就是每张图一个概率。参数量：G 3,576,704、D 2,765,633（torchsummary 输出）。

**训练两幕戏（注意顺序反转）**：

```text
for epoch → for batch（features 只有图，没有标签）:
  ── 第一幕：训 D ──
  random_vec = randn(128, 100, 1, 1);  fake_images = G(random_vec)
  real_loss = BCE(D(真图), 1);  fake_loss = BCE(D(fake_images.detach()), 0)
  optim_discr: 五步范式
  ── 第二幕：训 G ──
  gener_loss = BCE(D(fake_images), 1)      # 复用同一批假图，不 detach
  optim_gener: 五步范式
  ── epoch 末尾 ──
  images_from_noise.append(make_grid(G(fixed_noise)))   # 64 个固定噪声 → 8×8 网格
```

**Adam 的 DCGAN 修正**：[pytorch_ipynb/gan/dcgan-celeba.ipynb:L614-L621](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/gan/dcgan-celeba.ipynb#L614-L621) —— 两个 Adam 都传 `betas=(0.5, 0.999)`：一阶动量系数 \(\beta_1\) 从默认 0.9 降到 0.5。GAN 的目标随对手更新不断漂移，动量会带着「过时的方向」冲，减半后更新更贴近当前梯度。

#### 4.4.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么 \(z\) 要 reshape 成 \((N, 100, 1, 1)\) 而不是直接喂 \((N, 100)\) 的向量？

> **答案**：`ConvTranspose2d` 只接受 4D 的 \((N, C, H, W)\) 输入。把 \(z\) 看作 \(1\times1\) 的 100 通道「特征图」，第一个转置卷积（k4, s1, p0）就能把它放大成 \(4\times4\)——整个生成器从头到尾只用卷积算子，没有任何全连接层。这正是 gan-conv 用「Linear 投影 + Reshape」想要达成的目标的更彻底版本。

**练习 2**：`betas=(0.5, 0.999)` 相比默认 `(0.9, 0.999)` 改的是什么？为什么对 GAN 有益？

> **答案**：改的是一阶动量系数 \(\beta_1\)（梯度均值的衰减率）。GAN 里每个网络的目标都随对手的更新而漂移，是非平稳目标；\(\beta_1=0.9\) 的动量会把较旧梯度的平均值带进当前更新，方向震荡加剧。降到 0.5 让更新更依赖近期梯度，DCGAN 论文的实验发现这显著改善稳定性。

**练习 3**：本 notebook 的两幕戏顺序是「先 D 后 G」，u5-l5 与 gan-conv 是「先 G 后 D」。顺序是硬约束吗？

> **答案**：不是。两种顺序在数学上都成立，实践中都有大量成功案例（原始 GAN 论文甚至建议 D 每轮多更新几次）。真正的约束是**依赖关系**：dcgan 里第二幕复用第一幕生成的 `fake_images` 且不 detach，这要求 G 的损失计算发生在这批假图的计算图还活着的时候——代码组织必须自洽。对比两个 notebook 的变量流就能看出作者按各自顺序重排了依赖（u5-l5 练习 3 的结论在这里再次得到印证）。

## 5. 综合实践

**任务**：在同一随机种子下对比 `gan-conv`（BCE 卷积 GAN）与 `wgan-1`（Wasserstein 全连接 GAN）在 MNIST 上的训练稳定性——每 5 个 epoch 保存一次固定噪声生成图；再用 DCGAN 结构生成一张 64 样本网格图。

**先诚实声明混杂变量**：gan-conv 与 wgan-1 同时在**结构**（卷积 vs 全连接）与**损失**（BCE vs Wasserstein）两个维度上不同，直接对比只能得到「这两个配方整体谁更稳」，无法归因。建议把对照矩阵扩成 2×2——正好凑齐仓库现有 notebook：

| | BCE 损失 | Wasserstein 损失 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 全连接结构 | gan.ipynb（u5-l5） | wgan-1.ipynb |
| 卷积结构 | gan-conv.ipynb | dc-wgan-1.ipynb |

这样「同结构不同损失」「同损失不同结构」都能各得一组受控对比。

**阶段一：搭建统一的采样协议**（示例代码，适用于所有四个 notebook）：

```python
# 示例代码：固定种子 + 固定噪声 + 周期性存档
torch.manual_seed(42)
# ……（实例化模型与两个优化器，注意种子要在建模前设定，u1-l3）……

z_fixed = torch.zeros((64, LATENT_DIM)).uniform_(-1.0, 1.0).to(device)  # 各 notebook 的 z 先验不同，按其原样采样
snapshots = {}

# 训练循环内，每个 epoch 末：
if (epoch + 1) % 5 == 0:
    model.eval()                                  # 关 BatchNorm 的随机性（4.1.3）
    with torch.no_grad():
        imgs = model.generator_forward(z_fixed).view(-1, 1, 28, 28).cpu()
    snapshots[epoch + 1] = imgs                   # 事后用 make_grid / imshow 拼网格
    model.train()
```

注意：wgan-1/dc-wgan-1 的 `LATENT_DIM`（50/100）与 z 先验范围（\(U(-1,1)\)/\(U(0,1)\)）各不相同，按各自 notebook 的原样保留；对比的是「各自配方在各自协议下的稳定性」。

判读标准（本讲各节的结论落地）：BCE 组看双方是否贴 \(\ln 2\) 拉锯（4.1）、D 是否过度自信（4.3）；WGAN 组看曲线是否平滑、\(-\)discr_loss 是否随训练收敛、critic 是否塌缩成常数（4.2.3 dc-wgan-1 的病态）。

**阶段三：DCGAN 64 样本网格**。按 4.4.4 的 MNIST 适配版（或下载 CelebA 跑原版）训练后，用 `fixed_noise`（64 个）+ `vutils.make_grid(nrow=8)` 生成最终网格，并与第 5、10、20 epoch 的存档并排展示演变轨迹。

**预期结果**（待本地验证）：MNIST 上四个配方都应能产生可辨认数字，但稳定性排序预期是「WGAN 组曲线更平滑、BCE 组更震荡」（WGAN 论文的核心主张）；dc-wgan-1 若复现 4.2.3 的 critic 塌缩形态，其网格质量应明显偏弱——这本身就是最有价值的实验发现。最终用 3～5 句话总结：**结构卷积化与损失 Wasserstein 化，各自对稳定性贡献了什么？**

## 6. 本讲小结

- **卷积 GAN（gan-conv）**：生成器改为「Linear 投影 \(100\to3136\) + Reshape 成 \((64,7,7)\) + 4 层转置卷积」，判别器改为 2 层步长卷积 + 单 Linear 读出；正则化从 Dropout 换成 BatchNorm，判别器 logits 直出配 `binary_cross_entropy_with_logits`（u5-l1 配套规则），两幕戏训练数学不变，最终双方贴 \(\ln 2\) 拉锯（0.73/0.70）。
- **WGAN 四件套 + 节奏**：critic 线性输出（去 Sigmoid）、`wasserstein_loss = mean(y_true*y_pred)`、真图 \(-1\)/假图 \(+1\) 标签、每次更新后权重裁剪 \(\pm0.01\)（notebook 文档写 0.1，以代码为准）、critic 每训 5 次生成器更 1 次；critic 损失 \(\mathbb{E}[D(\text{fake})]-\mathbb{E}[D(\text{real})]=-\hat{W}\)，读数不再有 \(\ln 2\) 参考线。
- **权重裁剪是粗暴的 Lipschitz 约束**：裁剪过强会把 critic 压成近似常数函数——dc-wgan-1 的日志（两个损失都 \(\approx0\)）就是活生生的病态案例；WGAN 稳定性的代价由 critic 容量支付。
- **label smoothing**：`valid*0.9` 两行改动把判别器对真图的自信封顶在 logit \(\ln 9\approx2.20\)，防其碾压生成器；单侧平滑（假图标签保持 0）避免给生成器留次优退路；与 `0.5*` 缩放同属「削弱判别器」家族。
- **DCGAN 配方（dcgan-celeba）**：\(z\) 作为 \((N,100,1,1)\) 的 1×1 特征图、k4/s2/p1 整齐翻倍的转置卷积链、判别器无池化全步长卷积、`weights_init`（卷积 N(0,0.02)）、`Adam(betas=(0.5,0.999))`、两幕戏反转为先 D 后 G、`fixed_noise` 64 个噪声每 epoch 存 8×8 网格；`Normalize(0.5,0.5)` 在数据管线完成 Tanh 值域对齐，`drop_last=True` 保证固定长度噪声批量不错位。
- **读日志要认清形态**：MNIST 上 BCE-GAN 均衡是双方贴 \(\ln 2\)；CelebA 上判别器长期占优（D 损失 0.02～0.17、G 5～7）是高维真实数据的常态——损失形态没有普世标准，配方的意义在于把失衡控制在「生成器还能学」的范围内。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

本讲走完了 GAN 家族在 `pytorch_ipynb/gan/` 下的全部主要形态（仅剩一份未读的姊妹篇）。建议的后续路线：

1. **同套 DCGAN 换数据**：读 `pytorch_ipynb/gan/dcgan-cats-and-dogs.ipynb`——同一配方搬到猫狗照片上，观察数据分布变化对稳定性的影响，检验你在综合实践里总结的判读标准。
2. **生成模型收官后转向序列**：第 6 单元 u6-l1 将从 IMDb 情感分类开始 RNN 之旅；生成与序列在 u6-l4 的 char-RNN 文本生成中会再次相遇——那里的采样温度与本讲固定噪声评估是同一类「控制变量看质量」的方法论。
3. **顺藤摸瓜读论文**：WGAN 的权重裁剪病态引出 WGAN-GP（Gulrajani 等，2017，梯度惩罚），DCGAN 配方则是后来 StyleGAN 系列的起点——仓库虽未收录，但你现在已具备直接读懂它们实现的全部基础。
4. **动手方向**：把综合实践的 2×2 矩阵扩展成「+ label smoothing」的 2×2×2，或给 DCGAN-MNIST 加上条件标签（对照 u5-l4 的 CVAE 思路实现 cGAN），都是检验本讲掌握程度的好题目。

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. - `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.
